LESSON: WRITING 4.3.2 WRITING LETTERS OF THE ALPHABET

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.2 Writing letters of the alphabet
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.3.2 Writing letters of the alphabet, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Which letters of the alphabet do you know? 2. which letters of alphabet can you fingerspell? 3. how do you fingerspell letters of the alphabet?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.3.2 Writing letters of the alphabet together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: flexibility as learner creatively models the letters of the alphabet and accept correction

from others.

● Self-efficacy; as learner correctly reads and writes the letters of the alphabet.

69

Values:
● Respect:non- discrimination attitude as learner read letters of the alphabet in pairs and without disagreeing.

● Responsibility: excellence as learner models, writes and matches letters of the alphabet.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Social cohesion as learners work together in groups to model, trace, write and make patterns on letters.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Learner relates the skill of matching alphabet in upper and lower case with matching numbers with objects in

Mathematic Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Adapted course book, Signed audio visual clips, tracing books, Flash cards, charts (manual alphabet), pictures, digital

devices, coloring materials such as crayons, online resources
